name: Trial
label: Equal Vision
lede: A Seattle straight edge band fronted by a professional juggler made one album, broke up the next year, and has toured more as a dead band than it ever did alive.

eras.title: The juggler takes the mic
eras.text: Seattle in the mid-'90s was a grunge town, and Trial was a political straight edge hardcore band in it. Singer Greg Bennick had been juggling professionally since he was a teenager, and wrote songs about facing suffering rather than hiding from it.

years.h: Trial forms in Seattle around singer Greg Bennick
years.p: Greg Bennick and guitarist Timm McIntosh start Trial, a political straight edge hardcore band. Bennick had taken up juggling at 13 after being put in the wrong school minicourse; he'd picked coin collecting.
years.xp: Bennick's way into hardcore was a friend's cassettes of New York radio shows, which he first thought were terrible. His first show was [[Hüsker Dü|5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06]] in 1987, where he met Bob Mould and Grant Hart at a water fountain. For a [[Ramones|d6ed7887-a401-47a8-893c-34b967444d26]] show a month later, his mother forged him a birth certificate.

years.p: Trial's first record, put out by the anarchist collective CrimethInc.. Bennick told Punknews working with them was great, and he watched their zine grow from one guy in an apartment.
Trial's second release, pressed as a 7" at 33 RPM and a CD EP. It's later paired with Through the Darkest Days on one compilation LP.

years.h: Greg Bennick's forehead meets Timm McIntosh's headstock in Cleveland
years.p: Mid-set at a 1997 Trial show in Cleveland, Greg Bennick's forehead collided with Timm McIntosh's guitar headstock. Bennick told Punknews he bled badly.

eras.title: Months staring at walls
eras.text: Trial's one full-length came together fast in the studio and slowly on the page. Equal Vision released it, and a year later the band was done, split over where to go next and unhappy with the label.

years.h: Alexei Rodriguez learns Are These Our Lives? in three days
years.p: Drummer Alexei Rodriguez, from Catharsis, learned the whole album in three days and tracked it in a day and a half. Brian Redman played bass.

q: Still totally happy with it musically and lyrically.
years.h: Are These Our Lives? comes out on Equal Vision
years.p: Trial's only full-length. Greg Bennick spent months on the lyrics, but Equal Vision's first pressing ran without them in the insert.
years.xp:
Bennick told Punknews he'd spent months staring at walls, thinking of words. The record pairs its songs with quotes; he says the quotes were inspired by the songs, not the other way around.

The only thing he'd change: one phrase in "One Step Away". Later reissues on Panic Records restored the full lyrics and added liner notes, and Bennick says Equal Vision isn't authorized to reissue it.

years.h: Trial break up over the band's future and their label
years.p: A year after Are These Our Lives?, Trial split. Greg Bennick told Punknews it came down to disagreements about what the band should become and dissatisfaction with the label.

eras.title: A post-mortem existence
eras.text: Bennick turned his fixation on death into a documentary while Trial kept coming back for a few shows at a time. In 2009 the band lost its bassist.

years.p: Bennick co-wrote and produced Flight from Death with Patrick Shen, a film on how fear of death drives human violence. Narrated by Gabriel Byrne, it won audience choice for best documentary at the Beverly Hills Film Festival.

years.h: Trial reunite for Seattle, London and Budapest
years.p: Trial play three reunion shows in Seattle, London and Budapest. A compilation pairing Through the Darkest Days and Foundation comes out the same year.

years.h: Trial play the Burning Fight book release in Chicago
years.p: Trial play the release show for Burning Fight, Brian Peterson's book on '90s hardcore, in Chicago.

years.h: Trial headline Fluff Fest in the Czech Republic
years.p: Trial headline Fluff Fest on July 25, then play Antifest in Stockholm in August.

years.h: Bassist Brian Redman is killed in a moped accident
years.p: Shortly after the August shows, Trial bassist Brian Redman died in a moped accident. He had played on Are These Our Lives?

eras.title: More shows than the first time
eras.text: After two quiet years Trial came back harder than ever, with a thirty-date European tour and runs through North America. Bennick said he had to wonder what a real band was anymore.

years.h: Trial return: Rainfest, The Rumble, Tsunami Fest, Sound and Fury
years.p: After two years off, Trial play Seattle's Rainfest, Chicago's The Rumble, East Coast Tsunami Fest, a surprise New York show and Sound and Fury in Santa Barbara.
Trial tour Europe for thirty shows, more than they ever managed in the '90s. Panic Records' reissue of Are These Our Lives? is in print the same year.

years.big: A dead band that tours more than ever
q: I have to wonder what it means to be a 'real band'.
years.h: Trial play 15 North American shows in two weeks
years.p: Twelve years after breaking up, Trial tour North America: 15 shows in two weeks. Greg Bennick is also singing in [[Between Earth & Sky|eb394966-a942-4480-a896-9ecd2fd2847e]].

years.h: Trial's last show, at a New Age Records anniversary
years.p: According to Discogs, Trial's final performance was at a New Age Records anniversary event in 2018.
